entities.name: Echinococcosis
entities.description: A chronic zoonotic parasitic disease caused by larval metacestodes of cyclophyllidean tapeworms of the genus Echinococcus (primarily E. granulosus causing cystic echinococcosis and E. multilocularis causing alveolar echinococcosis), characterized by slow-growing visceral hydatid cysts or destructive infiltrative hepatic pseudotumors with prolonged latency.

entities.name: Direct Contact with Domestic Dogs Shedding Tapeworm Eggs
entities.description: Close contact with infected domestic canines acting as definitive hosts (e.g., petting dog fur, muzzle licking) harboring adult Echinococcus tapeworms in their small intestines and shedding microscopic eggs in feces.

entities.name: Ingestion of Food or Water Contaminated with Dog or Fox Feces
entities.description: Consumption of unboiled drinking water, raw vegetables, or wild-gathered forest berries contaminated with feces of wild foxes or domestic dogs carrying infectious Echinococcus oncospheres.

entities.name: Pastoral Sheep-Raising and Home Livestock Slaughter Exposure
entities.description: Occupational or community exposure in pastoral livestock-rearing regions where sheep, goats, or cattle act as intermediate hosts and offal is fed to sheepdogs, perpetuating the dog-sheep transmission cycle.

entities.name: Sylvatic Wildlife Cycle Exposure in Boreal and Northern Temperate Zones
entities.description: Exposure to wild carnivore definitive hosts (red foxes, arctic foxes) and small rodent intermediate hosts (voles, lemmings) maintaining the sylvatic transmission cycle of Echinococcus multilocularis across cold temperate and boreal northern latitudes.

entities.name: Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato
entities.description: A cyclophyllidean cestode species complex (primarily E. granulosus sensu stricto [genotypes G1-G3, sheep strain], E. canadensis, and E. ortleppi) causing unilocular and multivesicular cystic echinococcosis encapsulated by a fibrovascular host pericyst.

entities.name: Echinococcus multilocularis
entities.description: The fox tapeworm cestode whose larval metacestode proliferates aggressively via external microvesicle budding without a protective pericyst, infiltrating hepatic parenchyma and mimicking necrotic liver cancer.

entities.name: Echinococcus vogeli
entities.description: A neotropical tapeworm species endemic to Central and South America causing polycystic echinococcosis in human visceral organs.

entities.name: Echinococcus oligarthrus
entities.description: A neotropical tapeworm species endemic to Central and South America causing unicystic echinococcosis, utilizing wild felids as definitive hosts.

entities.name: Multivesicular Daughter Cysts with Spoke-Wheel Honeycomb Pattern on Ultrasound (WHO CE2)
entities.description: Pathognomonic multiseptated cystic liver lesion containing multiple internal daughter cysts separated by matrix, producing a classic wheel-spoke, rosette, or honeycomb acoustic architecture on ultrasound.

entities.name: Water-Lily Floating Membrane Sign on Ultrasound (WHO CE3a)
entities.description: Detachment and collapse of the laminated endocyst membrane floating freely within the cystic cavity, visualized on bedside ultrasound as undulating acoustic echoes resembling a water-lily.

entities.name: Anechoic Unilocular Cyst with Double-Contour Wall and Snowstorm Sign (WHO CE1)
entities.description: Well-defined, round, unilocular anechoic cystic cavity demonstrating a distinct double-line boundary wall and fine internal acoustic echoes shifting with patient repositioning ('snowstorm sign' of floating hydatid sand).

entities.name: Thick Hyperechoic Eggshell Calcification with Posterior Acoustic Shadowing (WHO CE5)
entities.description: Curvilinear, dense hyperechoic mural calcification surrounding an inactive, non-viable hydatid cyst, casting a continuous dense posterior acoustic shadow on ultrasound or computed tomography.

entities.name: Infiltrative Hepatic Mass with Geographic Microcalcifications and Central Necrotic Cavitation
entities.description: Heterogeneous, invasive hepatic mass with irregular borders, scattered nodular and ring-like microcalcifications displaying a geographic pattern, and a central ischemic necrotic pseudo-cavity characteristic of alveolar echinococcosis.

entities.name: Hydatid Sand with Free Protoscolices and Refractile Hooklets on Microscopy
entities.description: Direct microscopic examination of aspirated hydatid fluid revealing free protoscolices, rostellar hooklets, and degraded laminated membrane fragments.

entities.name: Spike in Peripheral Eosinophilia Above 20 Percent Following Cyst Fissure or Leakage
entities.description: Marked acute elevation in peripheral blood eosinophil count (>20-40%) on admission complete blood count triggered by micro-leakage or fissure of antigenic hydatid fluid into systemic circulation.

entities.name: Positive Echinococcus Specific IgG Serology by ELISA and Western Blot
entities.description: Diagnostic detection of serum IgG antibodies directed against Echinococcus antigen B and antigen 5 (for cystic echinococcosis) or recombinant Em18 and Em2+ antigens (yielding >95% sensitivity for alveolar echinococcosis).

entities.name: Elevated Serum Alkaline Phosphatase and GGT from Extrinsic Ductal Compression
entities.description: Marked elevation in cholestatic liver enzymes (alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase) with normal to mildly elevated transaminases, resulting from mechanical compression of intrahepatic bile ducts by expanding hydatid cysts.

entities.name: Classic Triad of Biliary Colic, Obstructive Jaundice, and Urticaria or Anaphylaxis
entities.description: Pathognomonic presentation of intrabiliary hydatid cyst rupture marked by acute right upper quadrant colic, fluctuating obstructive jaundice, and severe urticaria or anaphylaxis with hydatid membrane passage.

entities.name: Hydatid Vomica with Salty Expectorated Fluid and White Grape-Skin Membranes
entities.description: Sudden dramatic expectoration of copious salty hydatid fluid, hemoptysis, and collapsed white gelatinous membranes (grape-skin appearance) caused by intrathoracic rupture into a bronchus.

entities.name: Sudden Anaphylactic Collapse Triggered by Cyst Rupture or Leakage
entities.description: Abrupt life-threatening anaphylactic shock featuring diffuse urticaria, angioedema, severe bronchospasm, and circulatory collapse provoked by traumatic or spontaneous cyst rupture and peritoneal fluid spillage.

entities.name: Stony-Hard Non-Tender Hepatomegaly with Progressive Obstructive Cholestasis
entities.description: Palpation of an irregular, rigid, stony-hard liver mass in the right upper quadrant associated with progressive jaundice and cachexia, characteristic of the infiltrative pseudotumor of alveolar echinococcosis.

entities.name: Acute Onset High Spiking Fever and Sepsis Within 48 Hours Without Antecedent Rupture or Abscess
entities.description: Hyperacute toxic presentation characterized by high fevers (>38.5°C), rigors, and septic shock developing within 48 hours without antecedent allergic collapse or bacterial cyst infection, ruling out uncomplicated echinococcosis.

entities.name: Thin-Walled Simple Liver Cyst Under 1 Millimeter with Avascular Fluid and Negative Serology
entities.description: Presence of a paper-thin cyst wall (<1 mm) lacking double contours, completely devoid of internal septations, daughter vesicles, hydatid sand, or mural calcifications, with negative Echinococcus serology.

entities.name: Arterial Hypervascular Liver Lesion with Elevated CA19-9 or AFP and Absence of Microcalcifications
entities.description: Infiltrative hepatic lesion demonstrating intense arterial hypervascular enhancement without dense geographic microcalcifications on multiphasic CT, accompanied by markedly elevated serum tumor markers (AFP or CA19-9) and negative Em2+/Em18 serology.

entities.name: Amoebic Liver Abscess
entities.description: A hepatic cavitary infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica presenting with acute high fever, rigors, right upper quadrant pain, absence of eosinophilia, and thick 'anchovy-paste' pus without internal membranes or calcifications.

entities.name: Simple Hepatic Cyst
entities.description: A benign non-parasitic congenital liver cyst displaying an imperceptible thin wall (<1 mm), homogeneous anechoic fluid, complete absence of internal daughter vesicles or calcifications, and negative serology.

entities.name: Cholangiocarcinoma
entities.description: A malignant biliary epithelial neoplasm that mimics alveolar echinococcosis through infiltrative growth and central necrosis, distinguished by elevated CA19-9, arterial enhancement, and absence of geographic microcalcifications.

entities.name: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
entities.description: A primary hepatic malignancy distinguished from alveolar echinococcosis by early arterial phase wash-in and delayed wash-out on multiphasic CT, markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), and lack of dense microcalcifications.

entities.name: Albendazole Anthelmintic Chemotherapy
entities.description: Oral benzimidazole therapy (10-15 mg/kg/day taken with fat-rich meals) inhibiting parasite beta-tubulin polymerization; provides effective cysticidal therapy in small active cysts (CE1, CE3a <5 cm), peri-procedural spillage prophylaxis, and indefinite parasitostatic suppression in unresectable alveolar echinococcosis.

entities.name: PAIR Percutaneous Aspiration and Scolicidal Hypertonic Saline or Ethanol Instillation
entities.description: Minimally invasive ultrasound-guided percutaneous puncture, aspiration of fluid, injection of scolicidal agent (20% hypertonic saline or 95% ethanol for 15-20 minutes), and re-aspiration, indicated for active uncomplicated cysts (CE1, CE3a >5 cm).

entities.name: Radical Surgical Resection with Scolicidal Field Isolation
entities.description: Complete surgical removal of the intact hydatid cyst (pericystectomy or partial liver resection) using scolicidal-soaked packs to isolate the operative field, indicated for multivesicular cysts (CE2, CE3b), cysts with biliary communication, or resectable alveolar echinococcosis.

entities.name: Standard Antibacterial and Antiviral Regimens
entities.description: Conventional broad-spectrum antibacterial and antiviral agents, which lack activity against cestode metacestodes and fail to alter the clinical course of echinococcosis.

relationships.target: Direct Contact with Domestic Dogs Shedding Tapeworm Eggs
relationships.keywords: definitive host, dog contact, fecal-oral transmission, egg ingestion
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Echinococcosis is transmitted by direct contact with infected domestic dogs harboring adult tapeworms in their small intestines, shedding microscopic environmentally durable eggs adhered to fur or around the muzzle.

relationships.target: Ingestion of Food or Water Contaminated with Dog or Fox Feces
relationships.keywords: foodborne contamination, unboiled water, wild berries, fecal contamination
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Echinococcosis occurs through ingestion of unboiled drinking water, unwashed agricultural produce, or wild-gathered berries contaminated with carnivore feces containing infectious Echinococcus oncospheres.

relationships.target: Pastoral Sheep-Raising and Home Livestock Slaughter Exposure
relationships.keywords: pastoral farming, sheep-dog cycle, livestock offal, intermediate hosts
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Echinococcosis is strongly predisposed by rural residence in pastoral sheep-raising regions where domestic dogs are fed raw livestock viscera containing fertile hydatid cysts.

relationships.target: Sylvatic Wildlife Cycle Exposure in Boreal and Northern Temperate Zones
relationships.keywords: sylvatic cycle, red foxes, wild canids, rodent intermediate host, boreal endemicity
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Echinococcosis (specifically alveolar echinococcosis) is predisposed by residence or foraging in northern temperate and boreal ecosystems where wild foxes, canids, and arvicoline rodents maintain an intense sylvatic transmission cycle.

relationships.target: Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato
relationships.keywords: cestode, cyclophyllidean tapeworm, cystic echinococcosis, hydatid disease
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Echinococcosis is caused by the larval metacestode stage of Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato, which forms fluid-filled unilocular and multivesicular hydatid cysts encapsulated by a host fibrous pericyst.

relationships.target: Echinococcus multilocularis
relationships.keywords: fox tapeworm, alveolar echinococcosis, infiltrative metacestode, microvesicles
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Echinococcosis is caused by Echinococcus multilocularis, producing alveolar echinococcosis characterized by malignant-like infiltrative proliferation of microvesicles invading hepatic parenchyma and vascular channels.

relationships.target: Echinococcus vogeli
relationships.keywords: neotropical cestode, polycystic echinococcosis, South America, Central America
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Echinococcosis can be caused by Echinococcus vogeli, an etiologic agent of neotropical polycystic echinococcosis reported in Central and South America.

relationships.target: Echinococcus oligarthrus
relationships.keywords: neotropical cestode, unicystic echinococcosis, wild felids
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Echinococcosis can be caused by Echinococcus oligarthrus, producing rare neotropical unicystic echinococcosis in Central and South America.

relationships.target: Multivesicular Daughter Cysts with Spoke-Wheel Honeycomb Pattern on Ultrasound (WHO CE2)
relationships.keywords: WHO CE2, daughter cysts, spoke-wheel sign, honeycomb rosette, ultrasound staging
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Echinococcosis exhibits pathognomonic multivesicular daughter cysts with a spoke-wheel, rosette, or honeycomb architecture on abdominal ultrasound, diagnostic of active WHO stage CE2.

relationships.target: Water-Lily Floating Membrane Sign on Ultrasound (WHO CE3a)
relationships.keywords: WHO CE3a, water-lily sign, undulating membrane, endocyst detachment, ultrasound sign
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Echinococcosis presents with the pathognomonic water-lily sign on bedside ultrasound, caused by detachment and collapse of the laminated parasitic membrane within the hydatid cyst cavity in transitional WHO stage CE3a.

relationships.target: Anechoic Unilocular Cyst with Double-Contour Wall and Snowstorm Sign (WHO CE1)
relationships.keywords: WHO CE1, unilocular cyst, double-line wall, snowstorm sign, shifting echoes
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Echinococcosis exhibits an anechoic unilocular cystic lesion with a sharp double-line wall and internal shifting echoes resembling a snowstorm on patient movement, representing active WHO stage CE1.

relationships.target: Thick Hyperechoic Eggshell Calcification with Posterior Acoustic Shadowing (WHO CE5)
relationships.keywords: WHO CE5, eggshell calcification, acoustic shadow, calcified cyst, inactive cyst
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Echinococcosis exhibits thick curvilinear hyperechoic eggshell calcification with dense posterior acoustic shadowing on ultrasound and CT, diagnostic of an inactive, non-viable WHO stage CE5 cyst.

relationships.target: Infiltrative Hepatic Mass with Geographic Microcalcifications and Central Necrotic Cavitation
relationships.keywords: alveolar echinococcosis, geographic calcifications, pseudocavity, infiltrative liver mass
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Echinococcosis (specifically alveolar echinococcosis) presents on CT/ultrasound as an infiltrative tumor-like liver mass with dense geographic microcalcifications and central ischemic necrotic cavitation lacking daughter cysts.

relationships.target: Hydatid Sand with Free Protoscolices and Refractile Hooklets on Microscopy
relationships.keywords: hydatid sand, protoscolices, hooklets, microscopy, parasitic fluid analysis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Echinococcosis exhibits pathognomonic hydatid sand containing microscopic protoscolices and chitinous hooklets upon microscopic evaluation of aspirated or expelled cyst fluid.

relationships.target: Spike in Peripheral Eosinophilia Above 20 Percent Following Cyst Fissure or Leakage
relationships.keywords: peripheral eosinophilia, eosinophil spike, cyst leakage, antigenic stimulation, CBC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Echinococcosis demonstrates a sharp surge in peripheral blood eosinophilia (>20-40%) on admission complete blood count during or immediately following cyst micro-fissuring, leakage, or rupture.

relationships.target: Positive Echinococcus Specific IgG Serology by ELISA and Western Blot
relationships.keywords: antigen B, antigen 5, Em18, Em2+, IgG serology, Western blot
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Echinococcosis demonstrates elevated serum IgG titers on specific ELISA or Western blot detecting antigen B/antigen 5 (CE) or recombinant Em2+/Em18 antigens (AE).

relationships.target: Elevated Serum Alkaline Phosphatase and GGT from Extrinsic Ductal Compression
relationships.keywords: alkaline phosphatase, GGT, cholestatic pattern, extrinsic biliary compression
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Echinococcosis exhibits a cholestatic biochemical profile with elevated serum alkaline phosphatase and GGT caused by mechanical extrinsic compression of intrahepatic biliary ducts by the expanding metacestode.

relationships.target: Classic Triad of Biliary Colic, Obstructive Jaundice, and Urticaria or Anaphylaxis
relationships.keywords: intrabiliary rupture triad, biliary colic, jaundice, urticaria, hydatid membranes
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Echinococcosis presents with the pathognomonic intrabiliary rupture triad consisting of severe biliary colic, fluctuating obstructive jaundice, and urticaria or anaphylaxis with evacuation of hydatid membranes.

relationships.target: Hydatid Vomica with Salty Expectorated Fluid and White Grape-Skin Membranes
relationships.keywords: vomica, bronchial rupture, grape-skin membranes, salty sputum, pulmonary CE
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Echinococcosis presents with pathognomonic hydatid vomica, characterized by sudden coughing spells expectorating profuse salty fluid and gelatinous grape-skin membranes upon intrabronchial cyst rupture.

relationships.target: Sudden Anaphylactic Collapse Triggered by Cyst Rupture or Leakage
relationships.keywords: anaphylactic shock, circulatory collapse, cyst rupture, blunt trauma, antigenic fluid
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Echinococcosis presents with sudden life-threatening anaphylactic collapse provoked by traumatic or spontaneous puncture and peritoneal spillage of hyper-antigenic hydatid cyst fluid.

relationships.target: Stony-Hard Non-Tender Hepatomegaly with Progressive Obstructive Cholestasis
relationships.keywords: stony hepatomegaly, alveolar echinococcosis, obstructive jaundice, hepatic mass
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Echinococcosis (alveolar form) presents on physical examination as a stony-hard, non-tender irregular hepatic mass associated with slowly progressive biliary obstruction and portal hypertension.

relationships.target: Acute Onset High Spiking Fever and Sepsis Within 48 Hours Without Antecedent Rupture or Abscess
relationships.keywords: hyperacute sepsis, high spiking fever, toxic presentation, negative likelihood ratio
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by the hyperacute onset of high spiking fevers, chills, and septic shock within 48 hours in the absence of documented bacterial superinfection or anaphylactic collapse.

relationships.target: Thin-Walled Simple Liver Cyst Under 1 Millimeter with Avascular Fluid and Negative Serology
relationships.keywords: thin cyst wall, absence of daughter cysts, negative serology, simple cyst
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by ultrasound identification of an entirely unilocular thin-walled (<1 mm) hepatic cyst without double-layer contours, daughter cysts, or mural calcifications alongside negative Echinococcus serology.

relationships.target: Arterial Hypervascular Liver Lesion with Elevated CA19-9 or AFP and Absence of Microcalcifications
relationships.keywords: arterial hyperenhancement, elevated AFP, elevated CA19-9, absence of microcalcifications
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis (specifically alveolar echinococcosis) is ruled out by the presence of arterial phase hypervascular contrast enhancement on multiphasic CT, markedly elevated CA19-9 or AFP, and complete absence of microcalcifications.

relationships.target: Amoebic Liver Abscess
relationships.keywords: Entamoeba histolytica, anchovy-sauce pus, acute fever, lack of eosinophilia
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from amoebic liver abscess, which presents acutely with high spiking fever, severe abdominal pain, complete lack of eosinophilia, and thick anchovy-paste aspirate lacking internal membranes or calcifications.

relationships.target: Simple Hepatic Cyst
relationships.keywords: simple liver cyst, thin wall, lack of daughter cysts, negative serology
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from simple non-parasitic hepatic cysts, which display thin imperceptible walls (<1 mm), strictly homogeneous anechoic fluid, complete absence of internal membranes or eggshell calcifications, and negative serology.

relationships.target: Cholangiocarcinoma
relationships.keywords: biliary malignancy, CA19-9, hypervascular enhancement, central necrosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis (alveolar form) is differentiated from cholangiocarcinoma, which exhibits elevated serum CA19-9, hypervascular arterial contrast enhancement on triphasic CT, and lacks the pathognomonic dense geographic microcalcifications and positive Em2+/Em18 serology of alveolar echinococcosis.

relationships.target: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
relationships.keywords: primary liver cancer, AFP, arterial wash-in, venous wash-out, microcalcifications
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from hepatocellular carcinoma, which features elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), classic arterial phase wash-in with portovenous wash-out on dynamic CT, and absence of echinococcal calcific matrix.

relationships.target: Albendazole Anthelmintic Chemotherapy
relationships.keywords: albendazole, benzimidazole, beta-tubulin inhibitor, cysticidal therapy, parasitostatic
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Echinococcosis responds to albendazole chemotherapy (10-15 mg/kg/day taken with fatty meals), which inhibits parasite beta-tubulin polymerization, leading to cyst inactivation in small active cysts and preventing secondary seeding.

relationships.target: PAIR Percutaneous Aspiration and Scolicidal Hypertonic Saline or Ethanol Instillation
relationships.keywords: PAIR technique, percutaneous intervention, hypertonic saline, ethanol scolicide, CE1 and CE3a
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Echinococcosis responds to the PAIR procedure (percutaneous puncture, aspiration, injection of 20% hypertonic saline or 95% ethanol for 15-20 minutes, and re-aspiration) for active uncomplicated cysts greater than 5 cm.

relationships.target: Radical Surgical Resection with Scolicidal Field Isolation
relationships.keywords: pericystectomy, partial hepatectomy, scolicidal pack isolation, CE2, CE3b, radical surgery
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Echinococcosis responds to radical surgical resection (pericystectomy or anatomical hepatectomy) with meticulous intraoperative scolicidal field isolation, providing curative therapy for large multivesicular cysts and localized alveolar lesions.

relationships.target: Standard Antibacterial and Antiviral Regimens
relationships.keywords: antibiotic refractoriness, antibacterial resistance, antiviral ineffectiveness
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Echinococcosis is intrinsically resistant to standard antibacterial and antiviral regimens, exhibiting complete lack of therapeutic response in the absence of secondary bacterial superinfection.
